_why: Porch & Party Studio's niche brief (owner, 7 Nov 2026): the competitor research behind P&P captions v3 (https://claude.ai/artifact/UoyfsfFv43NpwmwNQur5kT), stored as the brief every writer reads. P&P is an existing studio, so no research job runs for it; this file is seeded once into its D1 (worker/lib/nicheBrief.ts seedBrief). Public pages only, read 7 Nov 2026.

brief.buyer: Someone in Memphis, Germantown, Collierville or Bartlett planning a surprise or a season for someone else: a partner's birthday or anniversary room (home or hotel), a shower or kids' party they are hosting, or a holiday porch they do not want to climb a ladder for. They buy the ease and the credit, not the decorations.
hooks: POV from the buyer's side: "POV: they think you did all this"
The person it is for, in their words: "He says he doesn't need anything"
A universal feeling said to the viewer: "We all deserve to walk into a decorated room one day" (3.0M plays)
The problem it solves, as a question: "Hosting the birthday and already tired?"
A true countdown: "Christmas is 7 weeks out. Your porch?"
Watch it come together: "Trust the process", "took 2.5 hours in 30 seconds"
caption_patterns: Never describe what the viewer can already see; add who it is for, the moment, the ease or a true reason to book now
The buyer is the hero: they get the credit, the business stays behind the scenes
Say the ease plainly: one form, set up while they're out, no ladder, takedown after
Name the real towns served for local proof
cta_patterns: One ask with one link: "Check your date: porchandparty901.com/request"
Competitors use "DM to book" and "January bookings are available. Contact us today"; P&P uses the request link only
Urgency only when true: a holiday countdown or "booking December dates now"
avoid: Describing the decorations on screen (petals, candles, balloons, garland)
Inventing a customer, a review, a booking count or "almost sold out"
Inviting anyone to visit, stop by or tour: there is no shop
Prices in clips or captions (P&P ruling 23 Oct 2026), though Memphis rivals post $175
Customer names, faces or house numbers; "insured" or guarantees
Pinterest (too local, owner 7 Nov 2026) and any voice over (owner 7 Nov 2026)

tiktok.norms: 10-30 s; hook on screen in the first 2 s; 1-3 emoji in the room's colors

instagram.norms: Reels 10-30 s; hook first; same caption rules

facebook.norms: The same reel; the caption carries the town and the one link
